title: Put ports around the registration core

task.text: `Registration` sends mail through `SmtpClient` and reads the system clock, so it cannot run without them.
Make it a hexagon: pure rules behind ports, infrastructure in adapters. `Wiring.create()` and every result string must keep working, and `SmtpClient` stays as the fake SMTP server.

items: `interface Mailer` with `void send(String to, String body)`.
`Registration(UserStore, Mailer, java.time.Clock)` keeps the rules and no infrastructure.
Adapters implement the ports. `Wiring.create()` assembles them.

checks.title: Invalid emails are refused without mail
Duplicates are refused without a second mail
A welcome mail goes to the new user
Registration receives its ports and a Clock
Registration runs on a fake store, mailer and clock
The store port decides what a duplicate is

hints.text: The rules should not know that mail goes over SMTP, that users live in a `Set`, or that time comes from the OS. Each of those is something the outside world provides.
Declare `UserStore` and `Mailer` next to `Registration` and pass them, plus a `Clock`, to its constructor. Move the `Set` into a `MemoryUserStore` and the `SmtpClient` call into an `SmtpMailer`.
